runs.reason:
The Czech Senate almost never decides a bill on a fixed calendar day when that bill is absent from the published plenary agenda and committee preparation has only just begun. Ordinary bills are assigned, reviewed by the relevant committee, and then placed on a later sitting inside the 30-day constitutional window; a same-week decision without that sequence is rare.

The Chamber approved the +CZK 13 bn amendment on 4 November 2026 and sent it to the Senate that day. The Senate’s own notice the same morning already fixed the 25 November sitting around consumer-protection, end-of-life products and electronic-evidence bills, plus European items and reports—not the health-insurance measure. On 19 November, after the constitutive session, ČT24 confirmed the 25 November agenda remains those five mostly ecological and consumer bills, with the continuation of the same sitting set for 9 December (comfortably inside the 30-day limit). The health committee itself was only reconstituted on 19 November. No subsequent report has added the insurance bill to the 25 November order of business.

The clearest way the “no decision that day” outcome could still fail is an eleventh-hour agenda amendment driven by the 1 January 2027 effective-date pressure the health minister has already flagged. That remains possible but would require both the organisational committee and the newly formed health committee to compress a process that the published schedule has already deferred.

### 3. Strongest Reason the Obvious Outcome Might Fail
There are two meaningful ways the YES outcome could fail on 25 November:
1. **Opposition to suspending automatic indexation:** In the Chamber of Deputies, ODS voted unanimously against the bill and TOP 09 ex-minister Vlastimil Válek sharply criticized it for freezing the automatic valorization mechanism in 2028. Because the ODS and TOP 09 club is the largest faction in the Senate (30 senators), they could rally enough colleagues from STAN or KDU-ČSL to return the bill to the Chamber with an amendment preserving automatic indexation—especially since Health Minister Adam Vojtěch admitted on 4 November that the Chamber would still have time before Christmas to outvote a Senate return before the 1 January 2027 effective date.
2. **Agenda / Timing slippage:** Because the Senate only constituted its committees on Thursday, 19 November, and both the Health Minister and former Health Committee Chair Tomáš Fiala are scheduled to speak at the "Efektivní nemocnice 2026" conference in Prague on 25 November, the bill might either be pushed to a second day of the plenary session (Thursday, 26 November) or deferred to a subsequent session before the 12 December deadline.

Balancing the cross-party support (ANO + STAN + KDU-ČSL), the composition of the Senate Health Committee, and the urgent 1 January 2027 effective date against the risk of an ODS-led amendment or a one-day agenda spillover, I estimate a 72% probability that the Senate approves the bill unchanged on Wednesday, 25 November 2026.

facts.fact: The Chamber of Deputies approved the amendment to the Public Health Insurance Premiums Act (Sněmovní tisk 235) raising state payments for state-insured persons by CZK 13 billion in 2027, with coalition MPs and part of opposition STAN and KDU-ČSL voting in favor while ODS voted against.

Health Minister Adam Vojtěch stated that he hopes the Senate approves the bill as passed by the Chamber, noting that if the Senate returns it, the Chamber would still be able to vote on it again before Christmas so it takes effect on 1 January 2027.

In addition to Boris Šťastný's amendment setting the 2027 assessment base at CZK 17,540 (CZK 2,368 monthly per state-insured person), the Chamber adopted an amendment by STAN MP Michaela Šebelová abolishing the 5% limit on health insurance fund contributions to patient organizations.
According to parliamentary records, the approved bill (Sněmovní tisk 235) was delivered to the Senate on 12 November 2026, giving the Senate 30 days from delivery to decide on it.
At its constituent session on 19 November 2026, the Senate re-elected Miloš Vystrčil (ODS) as Senate President, while the ODS and TOP 09 club remains the largest faction with 30 members.

On 19 November 2026, the Senate constituted its nine-member Committee on Health for the 2026–2028 term, electing Lumír Kantor (KDU-ČSL) as chairman alongside four senators from ANO, one from ODS, one from STAN, and Tomáš Fiala (Naše Česko).
The Senate announced that the 2nd plenary session of its 16th term begins on Wednesday, 25 November 2026 at 10:00 AM.
